confirmed.claim: processGatewayRefund calls adapter.refund BEFORE persisting any marker; the comment claims 'the adapter idempotency key (= refundId) make a replayed job safe at both ends' but the razorpay adapter only passes it as `receipt` (razorpay.ts:216), a non-deduping reference field — Razorpay's refund API has no idempotency on receipt — so an at-least-once retry after a successful gateway call but before markRefundProcessing re-issues the refund; Razorpay refuses the second full refund (nothing left refundable) with a 4xx, the job dead-letters, and the refund row is stuck 'pending' with gatewayRefundId NULL forever.
confirmed.scenario: Worker executes adapter.refund -> Razorpay creates refund rfnd_X and returns -> process crashes (or SIGKILL, or Redis blip) before markRefundProcessing commits. BullMQ retries: refund.status is still 'pending', adapter.refund fires again, Razorpay rejects ('refund amount greater than the payment amount refundable') -> gateway_error thrown -> 5 attempts exhaust -> dead letter. The later refund.processed webhook for rfnd_X cannot match (markRefundProcessed matches refunds.gatewayRefundId, which was never stored) and no-ops, so orders.paymentStatus stays 'refund_initiated' forever while the buyer's money was actually returned — merchant and auditor see a stuck refund with no gateway reference. On any future gateway allowing partial/duplicate refunds this same window is a double money movement. Fix: persist gatewayRefundId (or a 'dispatching' marker) before/atomically with the outbound call, or reconcile by amount+payment on the processed webhook.

contested.title: shipping.pincode_policy mode 'carrier' throws not_supported_yet instead of the §1.10/D13 cache-first registry check
contested.claim: Spec §1.10 and D13 mandate that 'carrier' mode 'consults the existing serviceability_cache via the carrier registry, cache-first', but checkServiceability throws a 422 not_supported_yet AppError for that mode — a scope-narrowing recorded only in a code comment ('per the B4 task'), absent from the commit-message deviation records.
contested.scenario: A merchant (or support engineer following the design doc) sets store_settings shipping.pincode_policy to {"mode":"carrier"} expecting cache-first carrier serviceability: every buyer's serviceability precheck and every checkout POST on that store then fails 422 'Carrier-based delivery checks are not available yet', bricking checkout store-wide until the setting is reverted.
